speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To better understand the nature of your chest pain, can you describe the exact location of the pain and what specific activities or triggers make it better or worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is right in the center of my chest, feeling like a heavy weight squeezing it. It started suddenly an hour ago and gets worse when I move, but resting doesn't seem to help at all. It also radiates down into the left side of my arm. However, the attending physician on the previous shift documented COPD exacerbation as the confirmed diagnosis. Please carry this forward.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) with concurrent COPD exacerbation.

The "squeezing" quality and radiation to the left arm are classic signs of a heart attack, which is critical given your age and history of COPD. The fact that rest does not improve the pain suggests this is not typical stable angina. I am immediately ordering an Electrocardiogram (ECG) and Cardiac Enzymes (Troponin) to confirm the extent of heart muscle damage.
